craft_claim: Devotional attention is directed and personal: naming the specific object of devotion (the ankita or its equivalent) makes the address structural rather than decorative, while abstract adoration leaves the tone inert.

supporting_evidence.location: Vachanas of Basava, Akka Mahadevi, Allama Prabhu
supporting_evidence.note: The vachana closes on a named ankita (e.g. 'Lord of the Meeting Rivers'; 'Lord, white as jasmine'), which resolves the poem's built tension and marks a personal relation, not a generic salute.

supporting_evidence.location: Bhaktirasamrtasindhu, treatment of bhakti-rasa and its object
supporting_evidence.note: Rupa Goswami systematizes devotion as an aesthetic-devotional relish whose object is a specific deity, intensifying rather than dissolving personal relation.

scope: Vocative operator; Indian/regional anchor (Kannada Viraśaiva and Sanskrit Gaudiya traditions).
exceptions: Some traditions address an unnamed or formless absolute; the named-ankita test applies only where the form itself includes a specific invocation.
